To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the degeneracy of the effective potential of the periodic models is responsible for the infrared fixed point of the correlation length, which in turn induces the scaling behaviour of the correlation length.

the degeneracy of the effective potential in the infrared regime induces a new fixed point and the definition of the correlation function in the infrared regime is crucial for the correct determination of the order of the phase transition.
the correlation length of the broken symmetric phase of the sine-Gordon model with periodic boundary conditions is finite, while the layered case is divergent.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the scaling of the correlation functions in a periodic model with a broken symmetry phase, which is characterized by the degenerate ground state.
the study of the phase transition of scalar field theories in one dimension, which is induced by a degeneracy of the effective potential.
the investigation of the correlation length scaling for periodic models with degenerate effective potential in the broken symmetric phase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation length in periodic models is always finite, while in models without periodicity, the correlation length is infinite.
a degenerate effective potential induces the infrared fixed point and that the correlation length is a useful measure of the type of the transition in periodic models.
the correlation length of the massive sine-Gorden model scales as a power law in the broken symmetric phase, whereas the correlation length of layered sine-Gordon models scales logarithmically.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the correlation length is an effective measure of the degeneracy of the ground states.
the degeneracy induced scaling is a general phenomenon in the broken symmetric phase.
the degenerate effective action induces a new scaling regime in the broken phase, where the correlation length is proportional to the temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the correlation length of a periodic scalar theory in its broken phase can be calculated by a simple scaling relation.
the correlation length can be used to distinguish between different types of phase transitions.
degenerate potentials induce scaling of the correlation lengths in a way which is different from the standard case of nondegenerate potentials.
